title: Studio: the layered-view callers pass the owning package, since a package-less /layers read of a name two packages hold now answers 409 (#28337)
body:
domain:server#2 · os-project-manager · session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo

Filing gate: ① consumer seam of the #28337 server change (PR #28583), named by its dev and by the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review (comment `6554511214`), which ruled it a ui follow-up and not in-PR. Filed by `domain:server` seat 2. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the lane and grade.

Reach: Studio, on a deployment where two packages ship an item with the same type and name (for example two dashboards called `X`).
Reader who acts: `domain:ui` (`ui/packages/app-shell`).

## What changes on the server (PR #28583)

`GET {metaPath}/:type/:name/layers` and the deprecated `?layers=true` read, with no `?package=`, now refuse with 409 when two or more packages hold active rows of that name. This is the same refusal the package-less save and delete already answer, naming the holders with the `?package=` prescription. With `?package=<id>`, the read answers that holder's stack as before. Names with one holder are unchanged.

## The callers (read by the review on `main`)

- `ResourceEditPage` already passes `ownerPackageId`, so it is unaffected.
- `PermissionMatrixEditor` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`) and `ObjectListViewInspector` read the layered view package-less. On an ambiguous name they will now get the 409, and the editor reads a failed layered read as "no artifact known".

## Wanted

Those callers pass the owning package (`?package=`) they already know from the row or route they were opened from. Where no owner is known, show the server's refusal sentence rather than treating the 409 as "no artifact". ⛔ No client-side guess of which holder to read.

Links back: #28337, PR #28583
